availability_sentence: You can visit San Pedro de Atacama year-round, and the standard tours are offered in every month, although summer storms and winter snow can close the high-altitude trips for a day or more.
availability_source: GYG listings for the featured tours show departures across the year; Chile Travel and the 2026 closure reports describe weather closures of high sites, not a closed season; SPACE's cold-season pause applies only to its Bucket list tours (June-August).

visit_profile.typical_visit: A stay of three or four days built from day tours: a four-hour sunset trip to Valle de la Luna, a dawn trip to El Tatio (about six hours, pickup around 4:30 to 5 a.m.), a ten-hour Altiplanic lagoons and Piedras Rojas day, a salt-lagoon afternoon at Cejar or Chaxa, and a two-to-three-hour evening of stargazing.
visit_profile.hours_outdoors: Much of each tour is outdoors at exposed stops, with vehicle transport between them; El Tatio and stargazing involve standing still in the cold.
bundled_sites: Miscanti and Miniques lagoons, Piedras Rojas and Laguna Chaxa on the featured full-day tour
Machuca village on most El Tatio tours
visit_profile.transport_part_of_experience: Yes for the high trips: the road climbs from about 2,400 m to above 4,000 m, and those roads are what storms and snow close.
visit_profile.seasonal_versions: Highland routes can be shortened or swapped on storm or snow days; some astronomy operators skip the nights around the full moon or run a Moon-focused session instead; SPACE pauses its Bucket list tours June to August.
visit_profile.shelter_checked: Tours travel by van or minibus between stops (featured listing: transport included). Telescope viewing and the scenic stops are outdoors; no listing promises a heated observing room.

factor_weights.why: December to March storms and June to August snow are what close El Tatio, the Altiplanic lagoons and Piedras Rojas; the lower sites near town rarely close.

factor_weights.factor: Cold at dawn and at night
factor_weights.why: El Tatio is visited at dawn above 4,000 m and stargazing means standing still outdoors; town lows average below 0 C in June to August, with about 20 to 23 nights a month below freezing.

factor_weights.factor: Moonlight on the night of a stargazing tour
factor_weights.why: A bright Moon washes out faint stars in any month; it changes every few days, so it is a date choice, not a month choice.

factor_weights.factor: Daytime heat in town and at the lower sites
factor_weights.why: Average highs in town reach about 31 to 32 C from December to February against about 22 to 23 C in June and July.
The January-February summer school holidays, the July winter break and the September 18 holidays are when many Chileans travel; a booking-ahead factor, not a measured crowd series.

seasonal_archetype_evidence: One balance period exists on the evidence (dry high roads and milder nights in April and October-November), with real alternatives: May and September for travelers who accept colder nights, December-March for the warmest nights and the Uyuni mirror with a storm risk, June-August for long cold nights. Two priorities in the split, so B, not C.

climate.source: Direccion Meteorologica de Chile (DMC) climate portal, station San Pedro de Atacama INIA (national code 220024, owner INIA, 2,416 m, -22.932 -68.213); annual reports RE2009 (daily rain), daily maximum and daily minimum temperature, years 2011-2025, read 2026-11-03
climate.method: mean of daily maxima and minima per month for each year with at least 20 valid days, then averaged across years; rain = mean monthly total over years with at least 25 reported days; frost nights = days with minimum below 0 C, scaled to a 30.4-day month. Not a WMO 1991-2020 normal: the station opened in 2010.
climate.cross_check: Atlas Agroclimatico de Chile (Universidad de Chile, 2017) for San Pedro: same seasonal shape, lower summer highs (28 C, temperatures 1958-1989); the difference is in the older period, not the direction. Reanalysis not published.
climate.plateau: No public monthly series found for El Tatio or the lagoons; the page gives the direction (far colder, more summer rain) and the El Tatio site's own statement that dawn temperatures can be below zero.

limitations: The town series is 2011-2025 from an agricultural station that opened in 2010, not a 1991-2020 WMO normal.
No public monthly series for the high plateau; its cold and summer rain are given as a direction.
No reachable monthly visitor or price series for San Pedro; no month is ranked as quieter or cheaper.
No public road-status feed; closures are announced on the day by Carabineros, the municipality and operators.
Forecasts beyond about a week are unreliable; the checker says which source it is showing.

experience_recommendations.el_tatio: any month at dawn; dress for well below freezing; snow closures June-August
experience_recommendations.stargazing: nights near the new moon in any month; April-November carries less cloud risk
experience_recommendations.valle_de_la_luna: all year on an afternoon tour ending at sunset
experience_recommendations.uyuni: mirror after the summer rains; full route in drier months (see sibling page)
